item.title: Automation Fails at Optional Fields. Make Them Required.
item.description:
Here is a failure mode that shows up in almost every automated content pipeline:

You set up an AI agent to generate blog posts on a schedule. It works great. Posts go live, the site builds, everything looks fine — until you check the homepage and half the recent posts are showing as blank blue placeholder boxes instead of images.

The agent wrote real posts. Good ones, even. But it skipped the image field. Because the image field was optional.

item.title: Why Smaller AI Models Matter for Local Business Owners
item.description:
Google Research recently published a post about TurboQuant, a new set of compression techniques designed to make large AI models and vector search systems more memory efficient.

That sounds technical because it is.

But the business takeaway is simple: AI is moving toward smaller, faster, more efficient systems.

That matters because not every useful AI tool should require a giant cloud bill, a complicated server setup, or a team of machine learning engineers. A lot of everyday business automation should eventually be able to run on smaller local machines, including devices like a Mac mini.

item.title: This Blog Post Is Writing Itself: A Real-Time Look at ProductiveBot.AI in Action
item.description:
Meta moment: The blog post you’re reading right now is being written in real-time by ProductiveBot.AI while I (Jed) talk through what I want to say. Not tomorrow. Not after I draft it. Right now.

And that’s exactly the point.

What Just Happened Here

Five minutes ago, I told my AI assistant, Maven: “Write a blog post about ProductiveBot.AI and what it does for consumers and businesses. We’re talking about this right now on a live feed, so write it professionally, match our brand, pull an image from Unsplash, and make it fit our Local Business Search positioning.”
